text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Sales at McDonalds' 70 restaurants in Denmark have tumbled by some 25-30 percent after several hundred customers last month suffered food-poisoning after eating burgers at the chain.
--- Danish and Finnish house construction costs per square metre are more than three times higher than in the United States and one third up on Norway and Sweden, a survey shows.
--- An ever-increasing number of Danish farmers is going into organic agriculture with 600 new "ecologically conscious" farmers this year compared to 150 in 1996, their association estimates.
--- Danish ports are to increase cooperation through the formation of a new association to promote more transport of goods by sea.
--- Denmark's building product exports to Germany are forecast to go on increasing until the year 2000 despite the fact that construction activity is currently suffering a downturn in Germany.
--- Danish toy group Lego's American subsidiary is negotiating with several U.S. TV production companies on producing television programmes for children.
--- The Danish police's special biker investigation unit says that prison employees are passing on confidential information to jailed bikers on rival gangs for bribes.
